etymologies.etymologyHTML: From black (color of forged iron) +‎ smith (related to smite).

quote.citation: 1640, I. H. [i.e., James Howell], ΔΕΝΔΡΟΛΟΓΊΑ [DENDROLOGIA]. Dodona’s Grove, or, The Vocall Forrest, London:  […]  T[homas] B[adger] for H. Mosley [i.e., Humphrey Moseley] […], →OCLC:
quote.text: The blacksmith may forge what Religion he pleases.

quote.citation: 1879, R[ichard] J[efferies], chapter II, in The Amateur Poacher, London: Smith, Elder, & Co., […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Orion hit a rabbit once; but though sore wounded it got to the bury, and, struggling in, the arrow caught the side of the hole and was drawn out. […]. Ikey the blacksmith had forged us a spearhead after a sketch from a picture of a Greek warrior; and a rake-handle served as a shaft.

definitions.definition: A blackish fish of the Pacific coast (Chromis punctipinnis).
